messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate params. The user wants forecast for White Plains for next week with temperatures in Celsius. We need to find latitude and longitude for White Plains. White Plains likely refers to White Plains, New York. Coordinates approx 41.0535°N, -73.7629°W. So latitude=41.0535, longitude=-73.7629. For forecast we need to specify "hourly" or "daily"? Probably daily forecast. Also need to set "temperature_unit": "celsius". The Open-Meteo API supports "forecast" endpoint. Let's check typical usage: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=...&longitude=...&daily=weathercode,temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min&timezone=auto. But we want next week. We can request daily for next 7 days. The API returns daily arrays. We'll request daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,weathercode. And timezone=America/New_York. Also maybe "start_date" and "end_date" but not necessary if we just get next 7 days.

So function call:

requests_get({
 url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
 headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json" },
 timeout: 10.0,
 params: {
   latitude: 41.0535,
   longitude: -73.7629,
   daily: ["temperature_2m_max","temperature_2m_min","weathercode"],
   temperature_unit: "celsius",
   timezone: "America/New_York"
 },
 allow_redirects: true,
 auth: null,
 cert: null,
 cookies: {},
 proxies: {},
 stream: false,
 verify: true
})

But the function signature expects params as an object with keys: latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't mention daily or other query parameters. However the description says "Query parameters for the GET request." and lists only latitude, longitude, elevation. That seems incomplete. But we can still pass additional keys; the function may accept them. The tool spec might be simplified. But we can try passing daily etc. The function signature shows params: { latitude?, longitude?, elevation? }. But we can add more keys; the tool might ignore unknown ones. But we need to provide daily and temperature_unit. Might need to use "params" as dictionary with all needed keys. Let's do:

params: {
  latitude: 41.0535,
  longitude: -73.7629,
  daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,weathercode",
  temperature_unit: "celsius",
  timezone: "America/New_York"
}

But the param types: daily is string? The API expects comma-separated string. So we can pass string. So let's do that.

Thus function call.
